reason: The gap is real, and every claim in the finding checks out against the files. (a) experiments/lb_poll/lb_poll.py only calls `competitions submissions -v` every 600 s and never downloads the LB. (b) ladder_wait.py is not tracked in git. (c) R12-A5 (round12/report.json) lets only the round's browser agent run tools/e10_snapshot.py. (d) r_ladder.json L5 defines POSITIVE as 'displays 0.954 and moved our team up inside the block, read at the first COMPLETE poll', but it names no tool, no owner and no attribution rule. (e) Our LB row moved from #210 (16:20Z and 17:01Z) to #217 (20:01Z) to #229 (22:46Z) with no new score of ours, so a stale baseline would mislead. (f) Probes 39 and 40 were submitted 144 s apart (poll.log). With K2 latencies of 7.36-7.54 h and 10-min polls, P(both COMPLETE in the same poll) is ~0.75. VALUE is modest but real. The read only decides which informed combos go at ~08:00Z (L5). The finals move only through L9's display >= 0.955, so the private effect is ~0. Still, without the rule the in-block clause cannot be read honestly: a snapshot taken hours later mixes in other teams' moves, and a joint 39+40 move gets assigned to a knob after the fact (post-hoc). The finding has no VALUE problem as a closed line in disguise. It adds no mechanism, touches no R8 or byte-identity issue, costs ~5-8 cheap LB downloads by the session that already owns the API (R12-A5), and fits before ~04:30Z (now 01:18Z). FEASIBILITY needs fixes the finding misses. (1) The command lacks the competition slug. The zip name is fixed, so each call would overwrite the previous one. (2) The LB may lag the submission status. (3) The LB CSV itself allows attribution and a freshness check, which is better than 'exactly one ref turned COMPLETE between downloads'. In all four snapshots our row showed SubmissionCount 40 and LastSubmissionDate 2026-09-26 00:02:18 (= #38, 0.953, not the best). At 22:46Z probes 39-41 were already pending, so both fields count only SCORED submissions, and the date is the latest scored one. (4) Later probes can move us only by beating the RUNNING team best, max(K2, earlier ladder scores), not K2. So a move is a strict, sufficient POSITIVE, and no move is never NEGATIVE.
fix: Pre-register in CONTEXT before ~04:30Z (main session only; narrow R12-A5 exception; at most 8 LB calls on 27 Sep; 60 s backoff on 429, 3 tries; never inside a W6-critical submit minute). (1) CALL: `python -m kaggle competitions leaderboard biohub-cell-tracking-during-development -d -p experiments/lb_poll/lb/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>/`, one new folder per call (the zip name is fixed). Make one baseline call at ~04:15-04:30Z, before any ladder score. Then make one call right after each poll.log header that first shows any ladder ref (56589025, 56589065, 56589423, 56592350) COMPLETE. (2) FRESHNESS: our row (TeamId 16810638) must show SubmissionCount = 40 + the number of COMPLETE ladder refs in the same poll, and LastSubmissionDate = the submit time of the latest COMPLETE ladder ref. If not, the LB is lagging: retry once after 3 min (this counts toward the cap). (3) ATTRIBUTION: compare consecutive fresh downloads. A move is attributable only if our SubmissionCount rose by exactly 1 between them, and LastSubmissionDate then names that ref. A rise of 2 or more (e.g. 39 and 40 together) means neither knob is POSITIVE by the in-block clause. Only the >= 0.955 display clause stays open for those refs. (4) MOVE-UP TEST: at least one team that ranked above us in the earlier download ranks below us in the later one, with an identical Score string and identical SubmissionCount. Teams whose count changed are ignored. (5) READING: a move means the ref beat the RUNNING team best (>= K2), so it is POSITIVE. No move is never NEGATIVE; NEGATIVE stays 'displays <= 0.953'. (6) LOG each call in CONTEXT: UTC, file name, our rank and block position, count and date, and the verdict. Commit the downloaded CSVs with the round.
realistic_gain: Procedural only. It makes L5's in-block clause readable honestly and without post-hoc attribution. It may steer 0-1 of the ~08:00Z combo slots: public ~0..+0.0002 unrounded, P(it changes a finals pick via L9) < 0.05, private ~0. It costs ~5-8 LB downloads (~2 s each) and one CONTEXT paragraph. It adds no runtime, mechanism or R8 exposure.
